newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenian risk profile stable ahead of poll - agency.
newsitem.headline: Slovenian risk profile stable ahead of poll - agency.

text.p: Slovenia's risk profile remains broadly stable ahead of the nation's third muulti-party general elections on November 10, credit agency Dun and Bradstreet's (D&B) Ljubljana representative said on Wednesday.
"The economy continues to display strong fundamentals, although downside risks remain," the agency said in its latest Risk & Payment Review.
D&B gave Slovenian an unchanged DB3a credit rating for October, placing it behind the Czech Republic and ahead of Poland.
The report noted a rise in the annual inflation rate could reinforce monetary pressures, however.
In September Slovenia's annual inflation rate eased to 9.4 percent from 10.3 percent in August but it remained above the 8.6 percent seen at the end of 1995.
"This, together with a sluggish EU economic performance, continues to impact negatively on the visible trade deficit - and on overall growth prospects for 1996," it said.
The government has said it expects GDP growth in 1996 to remain between three and four percent, on a par with 1995's 3.52 percent growth.
Slovenia's trade deficit rose to $762.9 million in the first seven months of 1996, up from $704.1 million in the same period of 1995.
